solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Don't go and clip them in wet weather

indicators.note: in says the shortened pronoun sits inside the word for wet weather

parts.note: wet weather is rain

indicators.note: clip means trim the pronoun them down to its colloquial short form, dropping its opening pair

explanation.surface: Advice to a hairdresser not to leave, and to trim someone's hair while it's pouring outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clip' looks like a haircut, but it signals shortening the pronoun to its colloquial form, which is then set inside the wet weather word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put is the opposite of leaving, so not going is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Stretches between bends

parts.note: a river's straight lengths between its curves have a particular name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gymnastics instruction, stretching while bending, but the bends are those of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: On a river, the straight lengths of water between one bend and the next carry this name.

clue.text: The farthest one will be from a bank

definitions.text: The farthest one will be from a bank

parts.words: The farthest one will be from a bank
parts.note: the bank is a river bank, and the point farthest from both banks is the river's centre

explanation.walkthrough: The bank sounds financial, but it is a river bank; the middle of the river is farthest from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of a river is the point at greatest distance from each of its two banks.

clue.text: Reformed ladies showing the highest standards

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of ladies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women who have mended their ways now display impeccable standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Principles or perfect models to aim for are the highest standards one can hold.

clue.text: Broken car phone in Escort

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of the two words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A damaged in-car phone sits in a Ford Escort.
explanation.walkthrough: Escort looks like the Ford car model, which fits the car phone surface, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies someone, especially a young woman, to supervise, which is what an escort does.

clue.text: Rushed a hide-out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of hide are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off to a secret hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an old verb meaning hasten, so its past tense means hurried.

clue.text: Latin American country holds an alternative view

indicators.note: holds means the country's name contains the other piece

parts.note: Panama is a country in Central America
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A Latin American nation takes a different stance on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an alternative view' reads as an opinion, but view is the definition: a wide vista.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken view of a whole landscape is a panorama.

clue.text: Managed to get central heating at the farm

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in getting central heating installed at their farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: It joins another for a breather

definitions.text: It joins another for a breather

parts.words: It joins another for a breather
parts.note: the two openings of the nose work as a pair for breathing

explanation.walkthrough: A breather sounds like a rest break, but it is one who breathes; each nose has a pair of these openings.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nose has two openings through which air passes, working together for breathing.

clue.text: Corrupt theologian in crooked deal

indicators.note: in places the theologian inside the rearranged deal
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of deal are jumbled

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a theologian

explanation.surface: A dishonest cleric is mixed up in a shady agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective for the theologian, but it is the definition; 'crooked' rearranges deal to ALED before the theologian goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled as an adjective describes spoilt eggs, so it means rotten or corrupt.

clue.text: Write numbers of chain letters?

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
nines are numbers

explanation.surface: An instruction to write out the numbers in a chain letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'chain letters' is not a mailing scam but the letters that spell a mountain chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pennines are a range of hills in northern England, so their name is spelt by a mountain chain's letters.

clue.text: Third mate to be furious about having taken the helm

indicators.note: about means the furious phrase surrounds the mate's letter

parts.note: to see red is to become furious

indicators.note: third points to the third letter of the word mate

explanation.surface: A ship's third mate is angry that he has been put at the helm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third mate' sounds like a ship's officer, but it means the third letter of mate, T, set inside SEE RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a vessel is to be at its helm, so having steered is having taken the helm.

clue.text: Stolen silverware used by restaurant cooks

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
plate is household silverware

explanation.surface: Stolen silver cutlery ends up in use in a restaurant kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a thing used by restaurant cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated cooking surface is equipment that kitchen chefs use daily.

clue.text: A bowed old soldier

parts.note: bowed suggests stooping with age, but here it means equipped with a bow

explanation.walkthrough: Bowed looks like bent over with age, but it means carrying a bow, as a soldier of old did.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman was a soldier of earlier times who fought with bow and arrow.

clue.text: It's obvious I'd enter the contest

indicators.note: enter means go inside the contest word

parts.note: an event is a contest in sport
I'd written without the apostrophe gives ID

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that it is plain they will sign up for the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is clear to see, so it is plainly apparent.

clue.text: Observed and heard making a scene

indicators.note: heard means we take the spoken form of the word scene

parts.note: a scene is a setting or a public display of temper

explanation.surface: Someone was spotted and overheard causing a fuss in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of see: something observed has been spotted.

clue.text: Lead, say, in hard rock

definitions.meaning: lead is an example of a dense metal
a loud aggressive genre of rock music

explanation.surface: A singer leads in a hard rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead looks like a lead singer, but it is the dense element, one example of a weighty metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dense toxic element, and the same phrase names a loud genre of rock music.

clue.text: Passing test, ran in, all excited

indicators.note: all excited signals letters stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner passed a test and came in all worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means fleeting, lasting only a short while, as a passing fancy does.

clue.text: Compelled to use pressure in extremity

indicators.note: in places pressure inside the word for extremity

parts.note: an extremity is an end
force is pressure

explanation.surface: Someone was made to apply pressure in dire straits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enforced is imposed and compulsory, so one is compelled.

clue.text: Notable decrease in volume

parts.note: notable is read as of notes, so the decrease is in loudness in music

explanation.walkthrough: Notable seems to mean remarkable, but it means of musical notes, a lowering of loudness in a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning gradually getting softer, which is a fall in volume.

clue.text: Area inside American bases

parts.note: the American bases are those of a baseball field

explanation.walkthrough: American bases sounds military, but it refers to baseball, whose infield is bounded by four bases.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the infield square marked by the four bases is named for its gem shape.

clue.text: Shout and dance, say

indicators.note: say means the word for a dance is spoken aloud

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A caller yells and dances at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to yell loudly, cry out.

clue.text: Belittles schoolwork, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: lessons are schoolwork

explanation.surface: A teacher disparages pupils' homework, so the rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something's importance is to diminish it, so belittling it.

clue.text: Taking flight and running fast

explanation.definitionFit: Airborne travel, and also any rapid motion, as when someone goes off at great speed.

clue.text: Order to start shooting in battle

definitions.meaning: a film director calls this to start filming
fighting, as in seeing ... in war

explanation.surface: A command to open fire in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooting sounds like gunfire, which battle supports, but it means filming.
explanation.definitionFit: The film director's call to start a take, and also military fighting.

clue.text: Article about that particular place

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerning one specific location.
explanation.definitionFit: There is the adverb for a place pointed to, as opposed to here.

clue.text: Determination that snail, say, is about to demonstrate

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Proof that a snail, for instance, is about to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'soon going to', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysis is the determination of a substance's components, as in chemical testing.

clue.text: A sign that Verne's captain has turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the name reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: Something portends that the submarine commander from a Jules Verne novel has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent foretelling something.

clue.text: Subdued, having arrived after it's finished

indicators.note: after puts the arrival piece behind the finished piece

parts.note: over means finished
came means arrived

explanation.surface: Someone turned up after it all ended and was crestfallen.
explanation.walkthrough: Subdued looks like downcast, but it is a past tense verb: defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome someone is to defeat them, so overcame is subdued.

clue.text: It had row upon row of rowers

definitions.text: It had row upon row of rowers

parts.words: It had row upon row of rowers
parts.note: the ancient galley had two tiers of oarsmen, one above the other

explanation.walkthrough: Row upon row seems to mean many rows, but it means two banks of oars stacked one above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient galley with two banks of oars, one stacked above the other.

clue.text: Not looking forward to daughter going to university

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Someone dreads their daughter leaving for university.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading means fearing what is to come, the opposite of anticipating it eagerly.

clue.text: Name for stones when placed round an entrance

indicators.note: placed round means the word for when surrounds the entrance

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A name is given to stones set around a gateway.
explanation.definitionFit: Agates are banded semi-precious stones, a variety of chalcedony.
